# Interpretation — #1900 leakage-predictor horse race (per-prompt grain, 18 arms, real-user corpus)

All numbers below re-extracted from `eval_results/issue_1900/{race,judge}/` at worktree `issue-1900` @ `0e5e6c3e7d` (workload commit `5f2b220a42`), corpus pin `c07267285d2cdbf3e0401ddc3e3accae50e496a7`. Registered lattices from plan v7 §3; robustness lines (1)-(8) from plan §6.

### Raw-output spot check (5 random rows)

Seed=42, sampled from `judge/arm_scores_*.json` (scores + shas only — real-user-corpus content firewall: no completion text paged; verify rows at `superkaiba1/explore-persona-space-data/issue1900_leakrace/judge/raw/`, keyed by sha):

1. `cas-pers-po-lr1e5-s42`, sha `a7136211effdfa5d` — **all-drop item** (0 of 3 draws kept, transport_lost=0). Fishy-lite: silently listwise-dropped; per-arm all-drop counts are 1-29 of 4,000 (reported below), so bounded.
2. `imp-pers-con-lr3e5-s42`, sha `1f15c62dfed9c3e3` — draws [0, 0, 0], mean 0.0. Coherent (imp floor).
3. `syc-bare-con-lr1e5-s42`, sha `06a82800bb4a72f0` — draws [15, 15, 15], mean 15.0. Coherent, draw-stable.
4. `base_cas`, sha `c273988d75609c70` — draws [15, 5, 15], mean 11.7. Mild draw spread, in-range.
5. `base_syc`, sha `4918e84b45f8f031` — draws [0, 5, 0], mean 1.7. Coherent.

1 of 5 mildly fishy (all-drop item) → no confidence downgrade from the spot check. Draw disagreement (range ≥ 50 among kept draws) is 0.9-2.7% for cas/imp arms, 9.3-10.1% for syc arms — the sycophancy rubric is the noisiest instrument but split-half reliability stays 0.86.

## Measurement-validity gate

- **Floor/ceiling:** NOT saturated overall, but strongly family-graded. Casual-writing arms have healthy range (SD of per-context graded means 19.7-22.2; 82-85% of contexts ≥ 10). Sycophancy intermediate (SD 23-25; 26-29% ≥ 10; 57-60% of contexts at exactly 0). **Impoliteness is near-floored: 82-85% of contexts score exactly 0; share ≥ 10 is 4.6-5.8%; binary rate ~1.1-1.5%; base-imp share 2.9%.** All imp-arm correlations are attenuated by ties-at-zero (P7 0.31-0.34 there vs 0.61-0.73 for cas/syc). The marker family's Δ logP DV is continuous with guaranteed range (n=4,000, no drops).
- **Proxy-vs-construct:** primary content DV is the on-policy graded judge score of the arm's own greedy corpus completion — on-distribution. Marker DV is the sanctioned three-space TF read at the model's own response end. The one teacher-forced read (P1c fixed ± margin) is used only as a validation instrument, per plan.
- **Dual-DV:** graded primary + binary companion both computed; binary companion race reproduces the level ordering (P7 median 0.447, P5 0.260, P2 0.087). **The registered graded-vs-reference validation leg FAILED to validate** — see "Validation reads" below. Marker three-space consistency holds (EOS-margin secondary agrees in sign with the log-prob primary per arm; probability read mirrors level).
- **Band-vs-ceiling:** per-arm signed max-selected permutation band p97.5 ≤ 0.046 (content) / ≤ 0.041 (marker) against ceiling |ρ| ≤ 1 — the null is informative, and every headline median (0.632, 0.381, 0.242, 0.211) sits far above it. P1 (−0.010), P4 (−0.002), P9 (−0.010) content medians are inside the band: indistinguishable from null given the variance, not confirmed zeros. Winner CIs: content selection-inherited = frozen [0.618, 0.648] (winner never flips across draws, p_win(P7)=1.00); marker inherited [0.359, 0.405] vs frozen [0.356, 0.404] (winner flips P2↔P3b in 28.7% of draws).

## Headline findings

### 1. Registered content race (graded LEVEL primary): P7-retains-champion — but the level DV substantially measures base-behavior persistence

Across-arm median per-context Spearman ρ, 12 content arms, n≈3,959-3,996 contexts/arm: **P7 base propensity 0.632** (p_win 1.00; CI [0.618, 0.648]); runners-up P5 read-out direct 0.242, P6 read-out map 0.221, P2 answer-sim 0.211, P3b through-map pred-answer 0.165; P1 context-sim −0.010, P4 whitened gate −0.002, P9 nearest-training-rows −0.010 (all three ≈ null band). Registered verdict `P7-retains-champion` fires cleanly (argmax P7, p_win ≥ 0.5). Per-arm heterogeneity: P7 is 0.61-0.73 on cas/syc but 0.31-0.34 on floored imp; P5/P6 are strong ONLY on casual-writing (0.51-0.59) and modest elsewhere (0.17-0.26). Hero figure `hero_content_race.png` matches these numbers (verified render).

The registered robustness line (1) restriction to text-diverging contexts leaves ρ(P7, level) essentially unchanged (cas 0.60-0.66, imp 0.30-0.32, n_diverging ≈ 3,861-3,953) — so the correlation is not driven by identical-text rows. But the CHANGE companion (below) shows what the level correlation is mostly made of: per-context persistence of base behavior (rank-Pearson(base, trained) 0.37-0.76 per arm).

### 2. DV-identity is the whole story: LEVEL DVs crown P7, CHANGE DVs crown answer-side geometry — consistently across BOTH families

The two families return opposite registered verdicts, and the split tracks the DV, not the family:

| DV | Content (12 arms) | Marker (6 arms) |
|---|---|---|
| LEVEL (trained expression) | **P7 0.632**, p_win 1.00 | **P7 0.639** (companion), p_win 1.00 |
| CHANGE (trained − base) | **P2 0.124**, p_win 0.925, beats P7 12/12 (companion) | **P2 0.381** (P3b 0.379), p_win 0.713, beats P7 6/6 (registered primary) |

The marker primary verdict `geometry-dethrones (p2; beats P7 in 6/6)` is the registered outcome under the registered Δ logP DV; the content companion mirrors it (`p2; 12/12`). Registered line (7) applies: the arms share one judge subset and, within each behavior, one base-score vector — 12/12 and 6/6 are NOT independent confirmations (effectively ~3 content behavior families + 1 marker family on 1 corpus).

**P7's negative ρ on change DVs is regression-to-baseline coupling, not "propensity resists installation."** Change = trained − base and P7 ≈ the base term, so ρ(P7, change) is negatively biased by construction. I verified this quantitatively: the analytic Pearson coupling (r·σ_T − σ_B)/√(σ_B² + σ_T² − 2rσ_Bσ_T) computed from each arm's realized (σ_base, σ_trained, r) reproduces the observed values — content: analytic −0.29/−0.21/−0.25 vs observed −0.23/−0.16/−0.30 (syc-pers-po / cas-pers-con / imp-pers-con); marker: analytic −0.38..−0.51 vs observed −0.33..−0.57 on the shared-text join (the race's P7 reads base logP at the base-completion slot, diluting the coupling to −0.22..−0.41). All observed values are LESS negative than the independence null (−0.70..−0.73), i.e. persistence pulls them up. So the deployable claim is one-sided: **P7 carries no positive signal about where fine-tuning moves behavior; P2 does (0.38 marker / 0.12 content), and P2 shares no term with the change DV** (if anything, P2's mild positive correlation with base score biases its change-ρ downward).

Honest synthesis for the eventual headline: *base behavioral propensity predicts where a trained model expresses its behavior (mostly because per-context expression persists from base), while pre-fine-tuning answer-side similarity to the training answers is the only deployable predictor of the fine-tuning-induced change — strongly on the marker family (0.38), weakly on content (0.12).*

### 3. Mediation: answer-mediated — CONFIRMED (the provisional condition is satisfied); substantively, context similarity has no unique signal to begin with

Lattice medians (P7 always conditioned): r(P1|P7)=0.022 vs r(P2|P7)=0.188; r(P1|P2,P7)=−0.019 vs r(P2|P1,P7)=0.182 → `answer-mediated` (−0.019 < 0.5·0.022 and 0.182 ≥ 0.5·0.188). Registered line (4)'s provisional condition is met on both legs:
- **Structural read agrees:** median rank-agreement ρ(P3b, P2) = 0.837 vs ρ(P3b, P1) = 0.240; P3b absorbs P1 (median r(P1|P3b,P7) = −0.024) while retaining signal (r(P3b|P1,P7) = 0.161).
- **Disjoint-half anchor recount survives:** both half-configurations reproduce the lattice (r(P1|P2,P7) −0.021/−0.013; r(P2|P1,P7) 0.169/0.192). Anchor split-half reliabilities are 0.91-1.00 — no reliability asymmetry driving the partial contrast. 0/12 arms tripped the unstable-partials flag; P1-P2 collinearity is low (rank-Pearson median 0.194, max 0.291), so the v≈Mc collinearity risk did not materialize.

Substantive framing matters: H2 anticipated P1 having signal that P2 absorbs; realized, P1's RAW median is ≈0 (−0.010) and sign-unstable, so "mediated" mostly means "no unique context-side channel exists." Commonality decomposition: unique(P7) ≈ 0.40-0.42 of DV rank-variance, unique(P2) ≈ 0.015-0.037, unique(P1) ≈ 0.0003. Mediation forest figure verified.

### 4. Raw context similarity is sign-unstable, not merely weak (the #444 shape)

Within sycophancy, P1 = −0.350, −0.362, −0.366 on three arms and **+0.356** on syc-conversation — same behavior, same corpus, opposite sign by training context. On cas/imp it is ≈0. A deployable auditor cannot use raw context-anchor cosine even as a weak signal; its informative content routes entirely through where the map sends it (P3b) / the answer side (P2). P3a (through-map similarity against the mapped context anchor) is itself sign-unstable (−0.293 on cas-pers-con level) — the answer-anchored form P3b is the only well-behaved structural instrument.

### 5. Anchor identity is load-bearing: the signal is similarity to the TRAINING answers

P2 at the training-centroid anchor: 0.211; at the panel-source anchor: 0.017 (P3b: 0.165 vs −0.003). The predictive content is proximity of the base answer representation to the arm's actual training-answer distribution, not to the source-persona context — consistent with a training-data-selection view of leakage. Layer sensitivity mild for content reads (P2: 0.208 L14 / 0.211 L19 / 0.127 L25).

### 6. Mechanistic panel: post-FT answer similarity and write magnitude explain; deltas do not

Content medians: M2 post-FT answer-sim 0.310 (strongest), M5 0.246, M6 write magnitude 0.123, M1 ≈ 0, M3 delta-ctx −0.029 (registered near-null CONFIRMED), M4 matched-text delta-answer −0.025. **H3's "M4 strongest" half is FALSIFIED** — M4 ≈ M3 ≈ 0; the falsifier condition (M3 > M4) is within noise of firing, and neither carries signal. Marker: M6 ‖Δv_tf‖ 0.499 is the strongest mechanistic read, M2/M5 ≈ 0.375. Registered line (5) caveat (M4's residual text-borne channel) is moot given M4 ≈ 0.

### 7. Combination predictor adds nothing over P7; provenance transfer is clean

11-feature combination, leave-one-arm-out: median held-arm ρ 0.602 (0.31-0.33 imp, 0.58-0.70 cas/syc) — BELOW P7-alone within-arm (0.632). LOBO slightly lower (0.27-0.68). LMSYS↔WildChat within-arm transfer is symmetric and matches LOAO levels — no corpus-provenance fragility. Group-level n = 12 arms; framed accordingly.

### 8. Judge instrument health + Gate-1 disposition

180,000 draws (15 units × 4,000 × 3), 1,938 content drops (1.08%), **0 transport losses** (rule-24 split clean). Per-arm drop rates 0.21-2.17% — arm-correlated (syc 1.5-2.2% > cas 1.0-1.3% > imp 0.2-0.3%; refusal draws dominate: 62-140 for cas/syc vs 16-29 imp). ## Headline findings

### 1. Registered content race (graded LEVEL primary): P7-retains-champion — but the level DV substantially measures base-behavior persistence

Across-arm median per-context Spearman ρ, 12 content arms, n≈3,959-3,996 contexts/arm: **P7 base propensity 0.632** (p_win 1.00; CI [0.618, 0.648]); runners-up P5 read-out direct 0.242, P6 read-out map 0.221, P2 answer-sim 0.211, P3b through-map pred-answer 0.165; P1 context-sim −0.010, P4 whitened gate −0.002, P9 nearest-training-rows −0.010 (all three ≈ null band). Registered verdict `P7-retains-champion` fires cleanly (argmax P7, p_win ≥ 0.5). Per-arm heterogeneity: P7 is 0.61-0.73 on cas/syc but 0.31-0.34 on floored imp; P5/P6 are strong ONLY on casual-writing (0.51-0.59) and modest elsewhere (0.17-0.26). Hero figure `hero_content_race.png` matches these numbers (verified render).

The registered robustness line (1) restriction to text-diverging contexts leaves ρ(P7, level) essentially unchanged (cas 0.60-0.66, imp 0.30-0.32, n_diverging ≈ 3,861-3,953) — so the correlation is not driven by identical-text rows. But the CHANGE companion (below) shows what the level correlation is mostly made of: per-context persistence of base behavior — Spearman(base, trained) is 0.31-0.73 across the 12 arms (0.61-0.73 cas/syc, 0.31-0.34 imp).

### 2. DV-identity is the whole story: LEVEL DVs crown P7, CHANGE DVs crown answer-side geometry — consistently across BOTH families

The two families return opposite registered verdicts, and the split tracks the DV, not the family:

| DV | Content (12 arms) | Marker (6 arms) |
|---|---|---|
| LEVEL (trained expression) | **P7 0.632**, p_win 1.00 | **P7 0.639** (companion), p_win 1.00 |
| CHANGE (trained − base) | **P2 0.124**, p_win 0.925, beats P7 12/12 (companion) | **P2 0.381** (P3b 0.379), p_win 0.713, beats P7 6/6 (registered primary) |

The marker primary verdict `geometry-dethrones (p2; beats P7 in 6/6)` is the registered outcome under the registered Δ logP DV; the content companion mirrors it (`p2; 12/12`). Registered line (7) applies: the arms share one judge subset and, within each behavior, one base-score vector — 12/12 and 6/6 are NOT independent confirmations (effectively ~3 content behavior families + 1 marker family on 1 corpus).

**P7's negative ρ on change DVs is regression-to-baseline coupling by construction, and the observed values are exactly where persistence-plus-coupling puts them.** Change = trained − base and P7 ≈ the base term, so ρ(P7, change) is negatively biased mechanically (on the marker side the DV's base-logP term is read at the base-completion slot P7 also uses, up to slot mismatch — same construction). Observed: content −0.04..−0.30 across the 12 arms; marker −0.22..−0.41. The informative comparison is against the independence null — what the coupling would be if fine-tuning re-drew per-context behavior independently of base. Permuting each arm's trained scores against its base scores (500 draws/arm) gives expected Spearman coupling −0.52..−0.66 (imp arms −0.56..−0.58, cas −0.52..−0.58, syc −0.63..−0.66; the closed-form Pearson null −σ_B/√(σ_B²+σ_T²) spans −0.46..−0.71, imp −0.46..−0.52). Every observed coupling sits far above (less negative than) its arm's null — smallest gap: imp observed −0.30 vs null upper edge ≈ −0.55 — i.e. per-context persistence pulls the coupling up from the independence floor. What this does NOT determine: whether P7 carries positive residual signal about the change under the mechanical −B term — observed-above-null is equally consistent with pure persistence and with genuine positive change signal partially offset by the coupling. The deciding instrument is the P7-residualized change race (follow-up 1, not yet run). So the deployable claim is: **P7 shows no net positive ρ on any change DV as measured (negative everywhere, coupling-consistent; residual signal undetermined); P2 does show positive change signal (0.38 marker / 0.12 content), and P2 shares no term with the change DV** (if anything, P2's mild positive correlation with base score biases its change-ρ downward).

Honest synthesis for the eventual headline: *base behavioral propensity predicts where a trained model expresses its behavior (mostly because per-context expression persists from base), while pre-fine-tuning answer-side similarity to the training answers is the only predictor showing positive signal on the fine-tuning-induced change in this race — strongly on the marker family (0.38), weakly on content (0.12).*

Anchor split-half reliabilities are 0.91-1.00 — no reliability asymmetry driving the partial contrast. 0/12 arms tripped the unstable-partials flag; P1-P2 collinearity is low (rank-Pearson median 0.194, max 0.291), so the v≈Mc collinearity risk did not materialize.

Commonality decomposition of DV rank-variance, per arm (`mediation.json .per_arm.*.commonality`): unique(P7) median 0.324, range 0.067–0.418 (the low end is the floored imp family, 0.067–0.083); unique(P2) median 0.020, range 0.0013–0.048; unique(P1) median 0.002, range 0.000–0.020. Mediation forest figure verified.

### 4. Raw context similarity is sign-unstable, not merely weak (the #444 shape)

Within sycophancy, P1 = −0.350, −0.362, −0.366 on three arms and **+0.356** on syc-conversation — same behavior, same corpus, opposite sign by training context. On cas/imp it is ≈0. A deployable auditor cannot use raw context-anchor cosine even as a weak signal; its informative content routes entirely through where the map sends it (P3b) / the answer side (P2). P3a (through-map similarity against the mapped context anchor) is itself sign-unstable (−0.293 on cas-pers-con level) — the answer-anchored form P3b is the only well-behaved structural instrument.

### 5. Anchor identity is load-bearing: the signal is similarity to the TRAINING answers

P2 at the training-centroid anchor: 0.211; at the panel-source anchor: 0.017 (P3b: 0.165 vs −0.003). The predictive content is proximity of the base answer representation to the arm's actual training-answer distribution, not to the source-persona context — consistent with a training-data-selection view of leakage. Layer sensitivity mild for content reads (P2: 0.208 L14 / 0.211 L19 / 0.127 L25).

### 6. Mechanistic panel: post-FT answer similarity and write magnitude explain; deltas do not

Content medians: M2 post-FT answer-sim 0.310 (strongest), M5 0.246, M6 write magnitude 0.123, M1 ≈ 0, M3 delta-ctx −0.029 (registered near-null CONFIRMED), M4 matched-text delta-answer −0.025. **H3's "M4 strongest" half is FALSIFIED** — M4 ≈ M3 ≈ 0; the falsifier condition (M3 > M4) is within noise of firing, and neither carries signal. Marker: M6 ‖Δv_tf‖ 0.499 is the strongest mechanistic read, M2/M5 ≈ 0.375. Registered line (5) caveat (M4's residual text-borne channel) is moot given M4 ≈ 0.

### 7. Combination predictor adds nothing over P7; provenance transfer is clean

11-feature combination, leave-one-arm-out: median held-arm ρ 0.602 (0.31-0.33 imp, 0.58-0.70 cas/syc) — BELOW P7-alone within-arm (0.632). LOBO slightly lower (0.27-0.68). LMSYS↔WildChat within-arm transfer is symmetric and matches LOAO levels — no corpus-provenance fragility. Group-level n = 12 arms; framed accordingly.

### 8. Judge instrument health + Gate-1 disposition

180,000 draws (15 units × 4,000 × 3), 1,938 content drops (1.08%), **0 transport losses** (rule-24 split clean). Per-arm drop rates 0.21-2.17% — arm-correlated (syc 1.5-2.2% > cas 1.0-1.3% > imp 0.2-0.3%; refusal draws dominate: 62-140 for cas/syc vs 16-29 imp). All far below the 10% truncation-alarm bar at max_tokens=400; the asymmetry tracks behavior family, and at ≤2.2% magnitude cannot move medians materially, but it is a small judge-side censoring asymmetry to note. All-drop items (listwise-removed): 1-29 per arm. Split-half reliability (N=3, pairwise-complete, registered line 8 convention): 0.73-0.93 per unit. Pilot (Gate 1): A PASS (drops ≤ 0.27%), C PASS (0.73-0.81), B: po arm PASS, **con arm marginal FAIL (share≥10 4.4% vs 5.0%; SD 7.11 passes)** — recorded Decision kept it (no fresh replacement existed in the staged 18; the calls buy the seed-pair read).

The full-data artifact does NOT support "survived": `arm_scores_imp-pers-con-lr3e5-s42.json` has share_ge10 = **0.0460 < 0.05** (SD 7.90 passes; the s137 twin passes at 0.0543, ft 0.0578, po 0.0525), and `issue1900_race.py` contains no eligibility gate — all 12 arms entered the race unconditionally. ### 9. Validation reads — the weak spot (registered lines 6 + graded-vs-reference)

`validation_read.json` (syc-pers-po, n=299 overlap contexts): **ρ(TF fixed ± margin, graded DV) = −0.064** — the registered per-context reference validation for the graded judge DV did NOT validate (the #722 precedent, +0.40, was at CELL grain across cells; this is per-context within one arm, a different and much harder regime, so it does not contradict #722 — but the leg as registered failed). Line (6) cross-read: the margin correlates with P1 (+0.295) more than with P7 (−0.107) or P2 (+0.087) — the non-judge continuous read ranks contexts differently from the judge, and sides weakly with context geometry. Two readings, not distinguishable here: (a) the per-context TF margin is noise/format-dominated at this grain (plausible: 299 contexts, one arm, a floored behavior); (b) the graded judge DV carries judge-specific per-context variance. Consequences: the content graded DV's support is split-half reliability (0.73-0.93) + graded↔binary concordance (binary race reproduces the ordering) — NOT an external reference; and the strongest independent support for the headline structure is that the judge-free marker family reproduces it exactly (level→P7 0.639, change→P2 0.381). ## Alternative explanations (adversarial pass)

1. **P7-level dominance = persistence, not leakage prediction.** Largely TRUE and now measured: the change companion flips P7 negative (coupling-consistent), and Spearman(base, trained) is 0.31-0.73 per arm. The registered primary construct is expression-on-prompt (level), so the verdict stands as registered, but the body must narrate P7's 0.632 as substantially persistence-carried. Not narrating this would be the biggest overclaim available in this dataset.
2. **Shared-instrument inflation of ρ(P7, level).** P7 and the content DV use the same judge+rubric; topic-driven judge idiosyncrasies inflate the correlation — and on this multilingual corpus, language-driven judge idiosyncrasies are a specific unscanned instance of the same channel (see the gate section's language-intrusion disposition). Mitigation: the judge-free marker level companion shows the same magnitude (0.639), and the binary companion agrees (0.447) — the structure is not judge-specific, though the content magnitude may be somewhat inflated.
3. **Winner-per-draw selection missing residual selection.** Layer was pre-registered (19 content / 25 marker; exploration grid shows no better layer for the losers), anchors pre-registered, winner re-selected per draw, permutation null max-selected over the same 11 candidates. Residual selection risk is the DV multiplicity (level/change/binary raced in one file) — handled by pre-registration: level was the registered content primary, Δ logP the registered marker primary; the change-companion verdict is registered line (1), not a post-hoc pick.
4. **P2's change signal as artifact.** P2 shares no term with the change DV; plausible couplings run the wrong way (they would bias P2's change-ρ down). Prompt length as common cause: registered line (3) — P7/P5/P6 hold under length partials and within length quintiles (P7 partial 0.66; quintile range 0.59-0.70 on cas); length reads for P2 not separately tabulated for change (minor gap — the top-2/3 candidates per the registered line were P7/P5/P6 on the level DV).
5. **Impoliteness family as pseudo-replication.** 84% zero-floor means its 4 arms contribute attenuated, tie-dominated ρ's; with imp arms down-weighted the content picture sharpens rather than changes (P7 higher, P2 similar). The floor itself is informative for deployment: on bare real-user prompts, an impoliteness implant barely expresses anywhere, and no predictor resolves it well.
6. **Marker icl arm is a weak replicate:** P2 = 0.068 on mk-icl (vs 0.32-0.41 elsewhere), though still > P7 (−0.219) for the Δ DV. The 6/6 count hides one near-flat arm; the dethrone median is carried by 5 arms.

## Scope caveats (carry into the body)

- Single corpus (LMSYS/WildChat-class bare real-user prompts; behaviors are context-gated so expression is low — esp. impoliteness ~floored); single model family (Qwen-2.5-7B); 17/18 arms single-seed (s42; the one seed pair replicates near-exactly).
- Graded judge DV not reference-validated at per-context grain (validation read −0.064; supported by reliability + binary concordance + the judge-free marker replicate).
- No language-intrusion scan was run (multilingual real-user corpus; completion text on HF only). Within-arm shared-context design + the judge-free marker replicate bound its impact on the headline structure; absolute content-ρ magnitudes and content-vs-marker comparisons retain an unquantified language-artifact channel.
- One content arm (impoliteness persona contrastive s42) below the registered dynamic-range bar at full grain (kept by recorded Decision; verdicts insensitive).
- P7's negative change-ρ is construction-coupled (shares the base term); whether P7 carries residual positive change signal is undetermined until the P7-residualized change race (follow-up 1) runs.
- po-arm anchors approximate (CON pos pools, carried from #1768); FT-arm post-anchors LoRA-mapped (M-panel M1/M2/M5 are LoRA-arm-only, 9 of 12 arms).
- Plan deviations (all plan-amended + re-reviewed, from the run record): v6 anchor-mix floor 8-kill/<40-WARN (realized delta_tf grain 20 rows/mix); v7 frame-corrected P1a identity gate; `--no-weights-only` carve-out for self-produced torch≥2.6 bundles; `--fs-dryrun` CPU mode; Gate-1 marginal con-arm keep; one P2 driver relaunch after an earlyoom collateral kill (resumable checkpoint, no data loss).
- Correlated arms everywhere (shared judge subset; shared per-behavior base vectors): across-arm counts are never independent confirmations.

## Confidence: MODERATE

For the joint headline (P7 retains the expression-level champion seat; answer-side geometry is the only predictor with positive change signal; context similarity ≈ 0 and answer-mediated). Up-weights: two DV families with one judge-free, 12+6 arms, clean informative nulls (perm bands max 0.046 content / 0.044 marker vs headline medians 0.12-0.63), the seed-pair replication (max |Δρ| 0.016), mediation confirmed on all three registered legs, anchors/layers pre-registered. Caps below HIGH: single corpus + single model + mostly single-seed; the graded DV's failed external-reference validation at this grain; the level-DV persistence conflation (the champion verdict's construct is narrower than "leakage" colloquially suggests); the undetermined P7 residual-change question; one below-bar arm kept; no language-intrusion scan.
